'''Tala''' is a language from the [[West Chadic languages|West Chadian branch]] of the [[Chadic languages|Chadic language family]].<ref name="Blench, Roger">{{Cite web |last=Blench |first=Robert |author-link=Roger Blench |date=2006 |editor-last= |title=The Afro-Asiatic Languages. Classification and Reference List |url=http://rogerblench.info/Language/Afroasiatic/General/AALIST.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131007050740/http://rogerblench.info/Language/Afroasiatic/General/AALIST.pdf |archive-date=2013-10-07 |website= |publisher=Roger Blench Website. Publications |pages=4–6 |language=en }}{{Retrieved|access-date=2016-11-30}}</ref><ref name="An Atlas of Nigerian Langages">{{Cite web |last=Blench |first=Robert |author-link=Roger Blench |date=2012 |edition=3rd |title=An Atlas of Nigerian Langages |url=http://www.rogerblench.info/Language/Africa/Nigeria/Atlas%20of%20Nigerian%20Languages-%20ed%20III.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160806024945/http://www.rogerblench.info/Language/Africa/Nigeria/Atlas%20of%20Nigerian%20Languages-%20ed%20III.pdf |archive-date=2016-08-06 |website= |publisher=Roger Blench Website. Publications |pages= |language=en }}{{Retrieved|access-date=2016-11-30}}</ref> The language is spoken in the central regions of [[Nigeria]], and had approximately 1000 [[Native-speaker|native speakers]] in 1993. The language is unwritten.

== Classification ==
Tala is part of the Guruntum (Gurdung according to the work of [[Roger Blench]]) group of the [[South Bauchi languages|South Bauchi language group]], and is thus similar to the [[Guruntum language|Guruntum]], Tala, and [[Zangwal language|Zangwal]] languages.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Blench |first=Roger |date=2021-01-01 |title=West Chadic classification 2021 |website=Academia |url=https://www.academia.edu/58551549 |access-date=2022-12-20 |archive-date=2024-02-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240224054226/https://www.academia.edu/58551549 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== General Information ==
The Ju language is spoken in the villages of [[Kuka, Nigeria|Kuka]] and [[Talan Kasa]], which lie to the south of [[Bauchi (city)|Bauchi]]. The village is in the Bauchi [[Local government areas of Nigeria|local government area]] in the [[Bauchi State|state of Bauchi]].<ref name=e25/>

Tala shares [[language border]]s mostly with other [[West Chadic languages]]; Zangwal to the west, Ju to the southwest, [[Guruntum language|Guruntum]] to the southeast, and the [[Gera language]] to the north and northeast. To the south, Ju borders the [[sprachbund]] of the [[Dulbu language]].<ref name=e25/>

In 1993, [[Ethnologue]] estimated the number of speakers of the language at a thousand,<ref name=e25/> and the [[Joshua Project]] has estimated the number of speakers at 2,000.{{cn|date=March 2024}}
